correctness.rationale: The tuple is jointly square-zero. Proposition 2.1 of arXiv:2609.37698v1 identifies its scalar derivative ball; the explicit map has norm exactly one by a golden-ratio singular-value calculation. A Möbius transform and Schur complement prove the scalar rational inequality. The displayed rational function has denominator bounded away from zero on the tetrablock, and a directly reconstructed positive contraction-defect identity controls its norm on the full Shilov boundary. Its amplification is the explicit self-adjoint 4-by-4 block with eigenvalues 1+rho, 1-rho, rho, -rho, giving exact norm (1+rho)/phi. The one-dimensional Parrott case follows from complete boundedness of scalar functionals. Finite exact checker verifies arithmetic only, and published geometric inputs are cited.

value.rationale: An existential counterexample from a nonconstructive operator-space separation is realized by fixed 4-by-4 matrices and a 2-by-2 matrix rational test of degree two, both written explicitly. The exact golden-ratio norm and sharp rho boundary quantify the first nontrivial matricial level; the Parrott block-size minimum identifies a natural finite resource threshold. This is a motivated complete constructive boundary result rather than numerical sampling or a generic specialization without quantitative content.
